help_p1:
1. In the Port Map tab, add the maps (.bsp or .vmf). You can also drag files, folders or archives (.zip, .rar, .7z, .bz2) onto the list.
2. Select a map and pick its addon from the list, or type a new name. Every map can go to another addon.
3. Port settings opens the options that change how the maps are ported.
4. Press Port. Two maps are ported at a time, and as soon as one ends the next one starts. Finished maps turn green in the list. Open the addon in Hammer and load the map.
help_p2:
• Sky, lights, ropes, water, sounds and glow sprites become their CS2 versions. Every glow sprite keeps its own texture and size.
• Entities that CS2 does not have become ones that do the same job, or are removed. Fires become CS2's own fire effects.
• func_detail and brush entities without inputs or outputs become plain meshes.
• Invisible walls made with clip textures stay player clips.
• Blend displacements keep their blending and textures stay in place.
• Decals sit on the surface they stick to.
• Animated textures keep playing.
• Lights keep the brightness they had in Source 1, the sun too.
• The map gets light probe volumes, each with a small white light room out of sight; they overlap a little and fade into each other.
• Materials that lit the map like lamps in Source 1 (texture lights) glow in CS2 and give the same light when the lighting is baked.
• The map's particle systems (its own and the game's) become CS2 particle systems.
• Glass with the refract shader gets a blurred, dark tinted look that works in CS2.
• A sky drawn from a cube texture becomes a normal CS2 sky, and surfaces that show it look into the sky.
• The map's color correction goes into its post processing, and under water the camera gets an underwater look that follows the shape of the water.
• Water that lit its surroundings in Source 1 gets lights over it.
• Bhop maps get the bhop script, bhop blocks, timer zones and spawn points the way CS2 servers expect them.
• The sun (env_sun) is drawn into the sky texture, at the spot the map shows it.
• The 3D skybox becomes a skybox map of its own, which the main map shows around it.
• Textures that vanished with distance in Source 1 (like grid lines) fade out at about the same distance.
• Graffiti decals that darkened and lightened the wall stay see-through.
• Lasers and beams scroll along like in Source 1. Sparks (env_spark), smoke stacks (env_smokestack) and electric arcs (point_tesla) become particle systems that look like the originals.
• Wireframe materials keep their color, and materials that CS2 has but draws wrong are taken from Source 1.
• Water made with another shader (like moving water) becomes real CS2 water.
• See-through meshes (glass, grates, water) do not block visibility.
• Weapon strips (player_weaponstrip) are done by the bhop script.
• Lasers and beams draw their own texture and make sparks at their ends like in Source 1. Glows keep the size they have in the world.
• Where two see-through brushes touch, the faces between them are removed, so the glass does not look brighter there.
• Smoke volumes (func_smokevolume) use their own texture and thin out near walls like in Source 1.
• Thin boost and gravity triggers are raised to 6 units so CS2 notices them.
• Sky brushes show the sky and the 3D skybox, hide what is behind them and cast no shadows.
• When the port ends you are told about anything that needs a look in Hammer.
help_p3:
On the Missing Assets tab pick the addon and its map and press Find Missing: the materials and models the map uses that are neither in the addon nor in CS2 are listed, and so are the materials the addon's models use. Search in Games looks for them in the installed games and the resource folders, and Add to Addon converts the found ones into the addon (only the selected rows when some are selected).
The Search Files tab finds any file by its name, and the files it finds can be exported into a folder. When you export a file, the files it needs (the textures of a material, the parts of a model) are listed first and you pick which ones go with it, then the folder.
help_p4:
Files that are in no source show up in red in the table. The same list is also saved next to the report as missing_vmat_ref.txt and missing_vmdl_ref.txt.
When the map did not pack a material but its compiler left a copy of it in the map, that copy is used.
A model whose material is found nowhere can not be compiled by CS2. With "Placeholder for missing model materials" on (Settings), the model gets a light gray placeholder material instead and is shown in yellow, with the name of the material that was not found. Once the real material is in the addon, it is put back the next time a map is ported into it or assets are added to it.
Maps (.bsp) in the resource folders (Settings) are searched last: the files packed in them fill in what is missing, for example from the map a ported map was made from.
help_p5:
The Tools tab converts files outside of a map: Material Converter, Model Converter, Image Converter, Translucency Mask Maker, Skybox Builder, 3D Model Converter, Foliage Converter and Texture Converter. Skybox Builder takes six face images, or one open cube image that it cuts into the faces.
Add files, folders or archives to the list (or drag them onto it), pick an output folder and start. A row with an arrow opens to show the files it also uses. The 3D Model and Foliage converters have Collision and Convex boxes for every model. The output folder is not kept when the program is closed.
help_p6: Models are decompiled to .qc + .smd and turned into .vmdl files. Animated models are converted separately, so their animations are kept.
